An abstract class is like a template or a partially complete class. It defines what methods a class should have, but doesn't provide implementations for all of them.

In your case:

Vehicle is abstract, meaning it's incomplete - it can't exist on its own
It has an abstract method start() - this means any subclass MUST provide an implementation for this method
It has a concrete method stop() - this is already implemented
When you write Vehicle v = new Vehicle(), you're trying to create an actual object from something that's designed to be incomplete. That's not allowed in Java.

To properly use an abstract class, you need to:

Create a concrete subclass that extends the abstract class
Implement all abstract methods in that subclass
Then instantiate the concrete subclass
This is a fundamental concept in object-oriented programming - abstract classes define contracts that subclasses must fulfill. what final code should i use
